news.headline: Former Madhya Pradesh health officer booked over fake MBBS degree after 16 years
news.story_lead: Former Madhya Pradesh health officer booked over fake MBBS degree after 16 years Sunil Singh was removed from his post after a health department inquiry found his degree fraudulent. Police registered a case on Saturday. Former block medical officer (BMO) of Birsa Community Health Centre in Balaghat district of Madhya Pradesh , who held the post for the past 16 years, has been booked for securing the government employment using a fake MBBS degree, police said on Saturday.
news.full_article_text: Former Madhya Pradesh health officer booked over fake MBBS degree after 16 years Sunil Singh was removed from his post after a health department inquiry found his degree fraudulent. Police registered a case on Saturday. Former block medical officer (BMO) of Birsa Community Health Centre in Balaghat district of Madhya Pradesh , who held the post for the past 16 years, has been booked for securing the government employment using a fake MBBS degree, police said on Saturday. According to officials familiar with the matter, Sunil Singh, the former BMO, was removed from the post in June after a state health department inquiry found he had a fraudulent degree. He was then posted at a primary health centre in Damoh, and has been on leave since July. Balaghat has been in the news for the deaths of 32 children from the Baiga tribal community since May 18, of which seven died during Singh’s tenure. Also Read | 4 students booked for securing MBBS admission via fake freedom fighter dependent certificates On Friday, the Supreme Court termed the deaths “most unfortunate” while hearing a petition filed by a local resident and sought responses from the Centre, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh governments on providing compensation for the victims. The state government has attributed the deaths to Measles Rubella and Malaria and announced financial assistance of ₹ 2 lakh each for the bereaved families. Balaghat superintendent of police Aditya Mishra said: “The health department of Madhya Pradesh conducted an inquiry following a complaint filed about five months ago. The probe team found he had a fraudulent degree. The department issued an order on October 9 directing that an FIR be filed against him. Following which, the FIR was registered on Saturday.” A case was registered under Sections 318(4) (cheating), 340(2) (forged documents) and 336(3) (forgery) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, police said. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Shruti Tomar I have spent over a decade chronicling Madhya Pradesh’s political and social landscape, covering politics, investigative journalism, crime, human interest, and government policy, blending sharp insight with ground‑level depth. I have closely tracked three assembly elections, three Lok Sabha elections, leadership transitions in MP while exposing governance lapses, tender irregularities, and flawed policy rollouts. My reports have revealed gaps in the Cheetah project, irregularities in medical education, rigging in recruitment exams, and loopholes in policy implementation. In crime reporting, I have moved beyond FIRs to map systemic patterns — from organised crime networks and gender‑based violence to custodial accountability — balancing urgency with sensitivity. My journalism is defined by a commitment to human interest. I have profiled the marginalised Bancchda community, documented atrocities against tribal groups, and highlighted efforts to preserve their culture through heritage liquor and revival of spiritual practices. I have reported on farmers struggling with failed MSP promises, giving voice to those often reduced to statistics in policy files. Passionate about field reporting, I have reported on rampant sand mining in Chambal and Narmada, pharmaceutical companies supplying medicines under altered names, the dire condition of schools and colleges, the plight of commercial sex workers, and skewed sex ratios in specific districts. Beyond deadlines, and as HT’s state correspondent and assistant editor in Madhya Pradesh, I engage with ministers, farmers, students, and activists, believing the best policy stories begin with a single human voice. A postgraduate in Journalism and Mass Communication, I also hold a diploma in sports journalism. Read More

news.headline: Delhi markets to reopen on Sunday amid protests, traders urge vigilance and security
news.story_lead: Delhi markets to reopen on Sunday amid protests, traders urge vigilance and security Delhi markets are reopening on Sunday amid fresh protest calls at Jantar Mantar, with traders urging tighter security as fears of festive season business losses grow. Several markets in Delhi have decided to reopen on Sunday, urging traders to step up security and remain vigilant amid a tense situation following Saturday’s crackdown and heavy security deployment across the Capital. The decision comes as the CJP and student groups have called for another round of protests at Jantar Mantar on Sunday, raising concerns over potential disruptions during the festive shopping season.
news.full_article_text: Delhi markets to reopen on Sunday amid protests, traders urge vigilance and security Delhi markets are reopening on Sunday amid fresh protest calls at Jantar Mantar, with traders urging tighter security as fears of festive season business losses grow. Several markets in Delhi have decided to reopen on Sunday, urging traders to step up security and remain vigilant amid a tense situation following Saturday’s crackdown and heavy security deployment across the Capital. The decision comes as the CJP and student groups have called for another round of protests at Jantar Mantar on Sunday, raising concerns over potential disruptions during the festive shopping season. Atul Bhargava, who heads the New Delhi Traders Association (NDTA), said that a fresh advisory had been issued to markets. “This is the festival season and a lot of stock purchases by traders have already been made. We have asked the markets to re-open today but they must increase the vigilance. Deploy people near entrances to check no rowdy element is creating ruckus. A lot of chaos was seen in Connaught Place on Saturday but we can’t keep asking people to shut their shops,” he added. “Looking at the ongoing protests & sensitive situation in and around Connaught Place on Saturday. We request everyone to be vigilant & cautious while re-opening on 11/10/26. Please keep your doors on guard and let us be alert and safe,” the advisory to the New Delhi markets reads. Deep Dive Sanjiv Mehra, who heads the Khan Market Traders Association (KMTA), said that Khan Market would remain fully open. “Yesterday, we kept the market on wait and watch mode. Shops were opened after closure of three hours. Police was able to contain the protest. We have decided to remain open on Sunday,” he added. Ashok Kalra, general secretary of the Sarojini Nagar market, echoed the same sentiments, citing fears of business losses. “Navratri have started and this is the peak sale season for us. Our market is fully open and we urge customers to come. Yesterday, we witnessed sharp drop in footfalls. We are also urging police and authorities to help ensure normalcy,” he added. Brijesh Goyal, who heads the Chamber of Trade and Industries, said that retail markets would remain partially open due to uncertainty in the wake of the protests. “There was hardly any business yesterday. Not just retail trade, but including service sector, hospitality sector, transport, tourism, business has been affected across. Closure of markets during the festival has given a huge shock to traders.” - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Paras Singh Paras Singh is a New Delhi-based journalist with Hindustan Times, where he serves as Deputy Metro Editor. He reports on urban governance, the Delhi government, the Delhi BJP, water management, the environment, communities and city life. He joined Hindustan Times in 2021 after beginning his journalism career at The Times of India in 2016, where he covered civic bodies, the water and power sectors, and urban infrastructure. Over the last decade, some of his reporting has led to significant public impact, with investigations into environmental violations, corruption and illegal industrial activity contributing to multiple judicial interventions by the National Green Tribunal and the Delhi High Court. A graduate of St. Stephen's College, University of Delhi, Paras studied journalism from the Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC), New Delhi. Having extensively covered the capital's evolving civic and governance landscape, his recent work increasingly explores Delhi's history, built heritage, urban evolution and the relationship between people and place, alongside continuing to report on governance and public policy. news.full_article_text: 2025 ruling ‘last nail in coffin’ of 1987 order on delay condonation: Supreme Court The Supreme Court bench said litigants must demonstrate diligence throughout the entire period before filing a delayed proceeding. The Supreme Court has hailed a 2025 judgment authored by Justice JB Pardiwala as the “last nail in the coffin” of its 1987 ruling that it said has been repeatedly invoked to secure condonation of delay, warning that an overly liberal approach to limitation has kept the country “driven back” for decades by allowing litigation to continue despite inordinate delays. Bench criticises repeated reliance on 1987 Katiji ruling A bench of justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu on Friday criticised the Supreme Court’s decision in Collector, Land Acquisition, Anantnag Vs Mst Katiji, which condoned a delay of just four days in filing an appeal, saying the judgment had since been treated as a “panacea” for virtually every application seeking condonation of delay. “Nobody considers what Justice Venkatachaliah wrote in 1994,” remarked Justice Datta, referring to a subsequent judgment by former Chief Justice of India MN Venkatachaliah that cautioned against allowing bureaucratic indifference to defeat the government’s own legal interests. “And the last nail in the coffin is Justice Pardiwala’s judgment in the Shivamma case,” he added. Justice Datta’s remarks underscore a judicial push towards stricter enforcement of limitation periods, with the court signalling that the need to do substantial justice cannot become a licence for litigants, including government bodies, to disregard deadlines and reopen disputes after years of inaction. Also read: Supreme Court to hold special sitting today on pleas against Delhi detentions, curbs on transport Court rejects Karvy appeals over delayed SEBI challenges The bench made the observations while dismissing appeals by Karvy Stock Broking Limited and its former chairman and managing director C Parthasarathy against orders of the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) refusing to condone delays in challenging penalties imposed by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) . “We are not going to go by any other judgment. We will go by our own judgment,” said the bench, referring to the principles laid down by the Supreme Court on how applications for condonation of delay and challenges to orders granting such condonation must be examined. It specifically referred to the court’s ruling in Sheo Raj Singh vs Union of India (2023), authored by justice Datta, which drew a distinction between explaining a delay in the first instance and scrutinising a lower court’s decision to condone it. “Condoning a delay is one thing, but sitting in appeal over condonation of delay invites different kind of scrutiny,” said the bench. Also read: Supreme Court closes 22-year-old case for constitutional limits on privilege, but leaves key questions open Court seeks to rein in liberal approach to limitation The 1987 Katiji judgment had advocated a justice-oriented and liberal approach to condonation of delay, emphasising that substantial justice should ordinarily prevail over technical considerations. It also stressed that litigants should not be denied a hearing merely because of a short, non-deliberate delay. But the principle subsequently acquired a reach that the court now appears keen to rein in, particularly where litigants seek to reopen proceedings after failing to act with reasonable diligence. In Shivamma (Dead) by LRs Vs Karnataka Housing Board, delivered in September 2025, Justice Pardiwala laid down that a litigant seeking condonation of delay must explain the entire period from the commencement of limitation until the actual filing of the proceeding. The court rejected the notion that the explanation need only cover the period after the prescribed limitation period had expired, underscoring that diligence must be demonstrated throughout. The judgment also refused to extend special indulgence to the State or its instrumentalities merely because their decision-making involves bureaucratic processes. It set aside a Karnataka High Court order condoning a delay of 3,966 days by the Karnataka Housing Board in filing a second appeal, reinforcing the principle that limitation law exists to bring litigation to an end and protect successful litigants from perpetual uncertainty. Justice Datta’s own judgment in February this year, in State of Odisha Vs Managing Committee of Namatara Girls High School, traced the tension between the liberal approach associated with Katiji and the court’s increasingly firm insistence on timely litigation. SC rejects Odisha government’s plea over delayed appeal In that case, the Supreme Court rejected the Odisha government ’s plea to condone delay, describing its conduct as “utterly lethargic, tardy and indolent” and holding that the explanation offered was “not an explanation but a lame excuse”. The judgment revisited the 1987 ruling and a 1987 decision in G Ramegowda Vs Land Acquisition Officer, in which Justice Venkatachaliah had acknowledged that government decisions were institutional and often slowed by procedural red tape. The court had then held that some latitude for governmental functioning was permissible, while cautioning that the law of limitation bound everyone. But Justice Datta’s February judgment pointed out that the same Justice Venkatachaliah had, within a few years, expressed deep frustration with the government’s continued failure to act promptly. Justice Datta’s February ruling observed that reading Ramegowda and Amateur Riders Club together left little doubt that the Supreme Court’s initial optimism about improving governmental conduct had soon given way to frustration. news.exam_corner_topic: After CJP, Opposition calls for protest, march to Supreme Court to demand action against SIR
news.headline: After CJP, Opposition calls for protest, march to Supreme Court to demand action against SIR
news.story_lead: After CJP, Opposition calls for protest, march to Supreme Court to demand action against SIR Opposition leaders accuse the government of suppressing dissent and are demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation. Opposition parties have urged people to join their next round of protests on Monday that will include an unprecedented march to the Supreme Court after security forces turned central Delhi into a fortress and clamped down on thousands of protesters to stop a Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led movement demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. INDIA bloc leaders said they will urge the apex court to expedite cases related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the Election Commission (EC).
news.full_article_text: After CJP, Opposition calls for protest, march to Supreme Court to demand action against SIR Opposition leaders accuse the government of suppressing dissent and are demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation. Opposition parties have urged people to join their next round of protests on Monday that will include an unprecedented march to the Supreme Court after security forces turned central Delhi into a fortress and clamped down on thousands of protesters to stop a Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led movement demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. INDIA bloc leaders said they will urge the apex court to expedite cases related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the Election Commission (EC). Congress general secretary K C Venugopal said, “We appeal to every Indian concerned about the survival of Indian democracy to join us in a massive protest march in Delhi on Monday - against the nationwide Vote Chori orchestrated by the Modi-Shah regime.” Deep Dive Venugopal, one of the key strategists behind the Opposition’s protest plans, added, “INDIA MPs, leaders, workers and all concerned citizens will be holding a huge protest march against Gyanesh & Co, and a delegation of our senior leaders will submit a memorandum to the Hon’ble CJI for his intervention in this crisis.” Also Read | INDIA bloc to hold mega protest in Delhi on October 12, TMC says Mamata Banerjee to join “In the history of the country, no political delegation has ever marched to the Supreme Court. It will be unprecedented,” said another senior leader, requesting anonymity. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi -led government of turning the “mother of democracy” into a “muzzled democracy”, while Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi challenged the PM saying, “We are surrounding you, and we are not going to back down.” Former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal said the country’s youth had awakened and demanded Kumar’s resignation. Trinamool Congress (TMC) chief Mamata Banerjee said protests would continue in Delhi. Kharge, who chaired the INDIA bloc meeting that finalised the protest plan, said the government was detaining people questioning its actions. “Our youth, students, lawyers, journalists, social activists, farm union leaders, YouTubers, content creators, everyone who is questioning this regime are being detained. The Modi Govt has turned the ‘Mother of Democracy’ into a ‘Muzzled Democracy’! The cowardice of the BJP-RSS is on full display today,” he posted on X. He said detentions, arrests, jail terms, lathis and pellets would not deter people from protesting. Also Read | CJP renews protest call as Abhijeet Dipke, Dhruv Rathee remain detained; Delhi Police cite ‘broken promises’ amid crackdown “Since the days of our Freedom struggle, the youth have been at the forefront of shaping the nation’s destiny. The Congress Party, along with the united Opposition, will fight this tyrannical regime, tooth and nail. We shed our blood to win India’s freedom. We will continue to fight, with every ounce of our strength, to defend our Democracy, our Constitution and the fundamental rights of every Indian,” Kharge added. Gandhi accused ruling establishment of trying to suppress the Opposition’s movement and said it would not back down despite the deployment of security personnel and detentions. “The core characteristic of these people is cowardice. Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, Mohan Bhagwat, Gyanesh Kumar and Ajit Doval, the villains of this story, are slowly finding the space closing around them. We are closing that space. Mr. Modi, do whatever you want. Call out all the police: 10,000, 20,000, 50,000... Arrest all the leaders. Arrest all the young people. Arrest us all. We are surrounding you, and we are not going to back down. Mark my words: we already have the information we need,” he said. Gandhi said the Opposition would continue to defend the Constitution and protect people’s voices, urging young people to continue protesting. Banerjee was detained in a police van and taken to Dwarka after she sat on a silent protest on South Avenue, outside the residence of TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee. She said she had wanted to go to Jantar Mantar to express solidarity with the protesting youth but was not allowed to do so. “We were not allowed, so we were peacefully sitting outside Abhishek’s house. I had a poster. The police didn’t allow it and put us in a prison van. Are we murderers and criminals that we have been put in a prison van?” she said. Also Read | ' Will come back stronger': CJP's Ajinkya Shinde calls fresh protest after Delhi Police crackdown on Jantar Mantar stir Banerjee said Gandhi had asked her to remain in Delhi for Monday’s protests. “We will participate to support students and youth. We will continue to raise our voice,” she added. CPI(M) general secretary MA Baby said on X that Keralam Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan and several others were “confined to police vehicles for hours” and “denied food and water and were not even allowed to take essential medications.” In Uttar Pradesh, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav said political parties across the country had questioned the EC’s functioning and demanded that Kumar resign. “As a constitutional body, its duty is to deliver impartial verdicts and uphold its credibility within the democratic framework..If there is any conspiracy or plot behind the Election Commissioner’s actions, it is being orchestrated by the BJP,” he said. On Friday, a 10-member Opposition delegation met President Droupadi Murmu and submitted a memorandum seeking Kumar’s resignation, the repeal of the 2023 law granting immunity to the CEC and election commissioners and an immediate halt to the SIR. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Saubhadra Chatterji Saubhadra Chatterji is Deputy Political Editor at the Hindustan Times. He writes on both politics and policies.

hindi_translation.story_lead: After CJP, Opposition calls for protest, march to Supreme Court to demand action against SIR Opposition leaders accuse the government of suppressing dissent and are demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation. Opposition parties have urged people to join their next round of protests on Monday that will include an unprecedented march to the Supreme Court after security forces turned central Delhi into a fortress and clamped down on thousands of protesters to stop a Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led movement demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. INDIA bloc leaders said they will urge the apex court to expedite cases related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the Election Commission (EC).
hindi_translation.full_article_text: After CJP, Opposition calls for protest, march to Supreme Court to demand action against SIR Opposition leaders accuse the government of suppressing dissent and are demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation. Opposition parties have urged people to join their next round of protests on Monday that will include an unprecedented march to the Supreme Court after security forces turned central Delhi into a fortress and clamped down on thousands of protesters to stop a Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led movement demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. INDIA bloc leaders said they will urge the apex court to expedite cases related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the Election Commission (EC). Congress general secretary K C Venugopal said, “We appeal to every Indian concerned about the survival of Indian democracy to join us in a massive protest march in Delhi on Monday - against the nationwide Vote Chori orchestrated by the Modi-Shah regime.” Deep Dive Venugopal, one of the key strategists behind the Opposition’s protest plans, added, “INDIA MPs, leaders, workers and all concerned citizens will be holding a huge protest march against Gyanesh & Co, and a delegation of our senior leaders will submit a memorandum to the Hon’ble CJI for his intervention in this crisis.” Also Read | INDIA bloc to hold mega protest in Delhi on October 12, TMC says Mamata Banerjee to join “In the history of the country, no political delegation has ever marched to the Supreme Court. It will be unprecedented,” said another senior leader, requesting anonymity. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi -led government of turning the “mother of democracy” into a “muzzled democracy”, while Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi challenged the PM saying, “We are surrounding you, and we are not going to back down.” Former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal said the country’s youth had awakened and demanded Kumar’s resignation. Trinamool Congress (TMC) chief Mamata Banerjee said protests would continue in Delhi. Kharge, who chaired the INDIA bloc meeting that finalised the protest plan, said the government was detaining people questioning its actions. “Our youth, students, lawyers, journalists, social activists, farm union leaders, YouTubers, content creators, everyone who is questioning this regime are being detained. The Modi Govt has turned the ‘Mother of Democracy’ into a ‘Muzzled Democracy’! The cowardice of the BJP-RSS is on full display today,” he posted on X. He said detentions, arrests, jail terms, lathis and pellets would not deter people from protesting. Also Read | CJP renews protest call as Abhijeet Dipke, Dhruv Rathee remain detained; Delhi Police cite ‘broken promises’ amid crackdown “Since the days of our Freedom struggle, the youth have been at the forefront of shaping the nation’s destiny. The Congress Party, along with the united Opposition, will fight this tyrannical regime, tooth and nail. We shed our blood to win India’s freedom. We will continue to fight, with every ounce of our strength, to defend our Democracy, our Constitution and the fundamental rights of every Indian,” Kharge added. Gandhi accused ruling establishment of trying to suppress the Opposition’s movement and said it would not back down despite the deployment of security personnel and detentions. “The core characteristic of these people is cowardice. Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, Mohan Bhagwat, Gyanesh Kumar and Ajit Doval, the villains of this story, are slowly finding the space closing around them. We are closing that space. Mr. Modi, do whatever you want. Call out all the police: 10,000, 20,000, 50,000... Arrest all the leaders. Arrest all the young people. Arrest us all. We are surrounding you, and we are not going to back down. Mark my words: we already have the information we need,” he said. Gandhi said the Opposition would continue to defend the Constitution and protect people’s voices, urging young people to continue protesting. Banerjee was detained in a police van and taken to Dwarka after she sat on a silent protest on South Avenue, outside the residence of TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee. She said she had wanted to go to Jantar Mantar to express solidarity with the protesting youth but was not allowed to do so. “We were not allowed, so we were peacefully sitting outside Abhishek’s house. I had a poster. The police didn’t allow it and put us in a prison van. Are we murderers and criminals that we have been put in a prison van?” she said. Also Read | ' Will come back stronger': CJP's Ajinkya Shinde calls fresh protest after Delhi Police crackdown on Jantar Mantar stir Banerjee said Gandhi had asked her to remain in Delhi for Monday’s protests. “We will participate to support students and youth. We will continue to raise our voice,” she added. CPI(M) general secretary MA Baby said on X that Keralam Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan and several others were “confined to police vehicles for hours” and “denied food and water and were not even allowed to take essential medications.” In Uttar Pradesh, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav said political parties across the country had questioned the EC’s functioning and demanded that Kumar resign. “As a constitutional body, its duty is to deliver impartial verdicts and uphold its credibility within the democratic framework..If there is any conspiracy or plot behind the Election Commissioner’s actions, it is being orchestrated by the BJP,” he said. On Friday, a 10-member Opposition delegation met President Droupadi Murmu and submitted a memorandum seeking Kumar’s resignation, the repeal of the 2023 law granting immunity to the CEC and election commissioners and an immediate halt to the SIR. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Saubhadra Chatterji Saubhadra Chatterji is Deputy Political Editor at the Hindustan Times. He writes on both politics and policies.

news.headline: Young men live in fear of being snatched off the streets and sold to Myanmar's army
news.story_lead: Authorities in Myanmar have been ordered to aggressively fulfil the military's recruitment quotas, leading to corruption, extortion and abductions - Published 2 hours ago You do not stay out after dark if you're young and able-bodied in Hpa-An, the capital of Myanmar's southern Karen state. In recent months this has become conventional wisdom. But Zaw Min has no choice.
news.full_article_text: Authorities in Myanmar have been ordered to aggressively fulfil the military's recruitment quotas, leading to corruption, extortion and abductions - Published 2 hours ago You do not stay out after dark if you're young and able-bodied in Hpa-An, the capital of Myanmar's southern Karen state. In recent months this has become conventional wisdom. But Zaw Min has no choice. "I worry, but I have to go out to work," says the 26-year-old tuk tuk driver, who asked that his real name be omitted out of fear for his safety. "My family call me all the time and remind me not to drive passengers too far; to be careful who I take as a passenger... I have to be vigilant all the time. "People are panicked and frightened," he explains. "Some people I know have been taken." Locals say plain-clothed members and supporters of the Myanmar junta have been roaming the streets of Hpa-An, arbitrarily arresting people in their teens, 20s and 30s and forcing them into military service. According to leaked documents seen by BBC Burmese, authorities have been ordered to aggressively fulfil the military's recruitment quotas across jurisdictions, bolstering the junta's ranks as it endures a war of attrition against ethnic militias, pro-democracy groups and civilian-led resistance movements. Zaw Min is the only one among his siblings who is at the age of recruitment. Many other "kids" his age have fled, he says â to Thailand, or the homes of relatives further afield. Those who remain are often under strict instructions from their parents: be home before dusk. Myanmar has been locked in a bloody civil war since February 2021, when its own military launched a coup d'etat and ousted democratically elected leader Aung San Suu Kyi. Three years later, following a string of humiliating losses, plummeting morale and soaring rates of desertion, the junta enacted a mandatory conscription law that required all men aged 18 to 35 and women aged 18 to 27 to serve at least two years under military command. Those who refuse face up to five years in prison. The enactment of the law "represents one of the most severe and impactful actions taken against the entire civilian population since the military coup", according to Maj Naung Yoe, military affairs official at the Myanmar Defense and Security Institute (MDSI) and a former military officer who defected and joined the anti-coup Civil Disobedience Movement. An estimated 100,000 young recruits have been conscriptedby the junta since early 2024 Hpa-An is the latest to be caught in a dragnet that's already ensnared an estimated 100,000 young recruits over the past two-and-a-half years â many of them via coercion, extortion and abductions. "Security forces track young people's movements to arrest them, force them into service under the pretext of statutory military eligibility, extort money through threats of detention, and arrest individuals during guest-list inspections," Naung Yoe says. The BBC contacted the Myanmar government's Central Body for Summoning People's Military Servants regarding incidents mentioned in this story, including the forced recruitment of conscripts and reports of abductions allegedly carried out in recent months. They said they had no comment on the matter. With the mandatory conscription law, the junta has established a human supply chain to sustain its armed forces. And it appears to have worked. Observers note that reinforcements have played a critical role in helping the regime claw back more territory. In many parts of Myanmar, the resistance is now on the back foot. The war, though, is far from over. And as more youths evade conscription â either to join the resistance or simply avoid armed conflict against their fellow countrymen â the junta's recruitment methods have become ever more extreme. International rights groups such as Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch and Fortify Rights say Myanmar's military is abducting civilians and forcing them into military service. In July, open-source research organisation Myanmar Witness revealed that they had analysed hundreds of missing-person advertisements collected from Facebook between 2021 and 2025. Researchers found that missing person notices for January rose from four in 2021, pre-coup, to 82 in 2025, post-conscription law. "In practice, much of [the Myanmar military's] recruitment appears to be carried out through detention, coercion, and disappearance rather than formal call-up, and often without notice to families," they concluded. Men and boys constituted the majority of reported missing persons. Watch: BBC goes into jungle with Myanmar's civil war rebels "They are spreading rumours all over the neighbourhood that I sold my husband." Ma Moe San Pan sobs the words through gulps of air. She is sitting in her kitchen, at home in Yangon, where on the morning of 8 May 2025 she saw her 33-year-old husband Phyo Wai for the last time. "We had an argument, and afterwards he left home," she recalls."I was upset and told my cousin about what had happened." Ma Moe San Pan's cousin worked at the local ward administration office, and she asked him to bring her husband back. It was two days later that Phyo Wai called her, from a military recruitment centre on the other side of the city. The cousin had taken him to the ward office which had sold him on to another ward for 4 million kyats ($900; Â£680) to fill that ward's recruitment quota, Ma Moe San Pan says. The BBC was unable to reach Ma Moe San Pan's cousin. In a desperate attempt to bring him back, Ma Moe San Pan was then scammed out of 4.5 million kyats by strangers who falsely promised his release. U Maung Maung Lwin, the administrator of the ward to which Phyo Wai was taken, later admitted to the BBC that he had played a role in sending him to the military recruitment authorities. When asked about allegations that individuals were being conscripted outside their home township, he said transfers from other townships do occur when local quotas cannot be met. But he denied that any money was involved in such cases, or in Phyo Wai's forced conscription. "[Phyo Wai] told me they said they would help him and made him sign documents," Ma Moe San Pan recalls. "If my husband had been legally selected for conscription through the normal process, I could have accepted that. What I cannot accept is that our own ward administration office allegedly sold him to another ward. "I also regret placing my trust in my cousin." Ma Moe San Pan says her husband was sold into military service by her own cousin In the time since Phyo Wai was taken, Ma Moe San Pan has filed police complaints relating to two matters: the sale of her husband into military service, and the 4.5 million kyats she lost to scammers. The police accepted her complaint, she says, but refused her request to include human trafficking charges, claiming a human trafficking case could only be registered if a person had been sold abroad. She does not know where her husband is now. Ma Moe

news.headline: Allahabad HC warns against misuse of criminal law in short-lived marriages, quashes dowry FIR
news.story_lead: Allahabad HC warns against misuse of criminal law in short-lived marriages, quashes dowry FIR Prayagraj, The Allahabad High Court has warned that routinely turning every distressed or failed marriage into a criminal case could affect the institution of marriage at its core, quashing an FIR alleging dowry harassment, physical assault and attempted strangulation in a case involving a brief period of cohabitation. A division bench of Justices Chandra Dhari Singh and Tarun Saxena quashed the FIR registered at the Hari Parvat police station in Agra under various provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Dowry Prohibition Act, allowing a writ petition filed by Gaurav Jain and his family members. Emphasising the dangers of converting matrimonial discord intro criminal cases, the court cautioned against the misuse of criminal law in short-lived marriages.
news.full_article_text: Allahabad HC warns against misuse of criminal law in short-lived marriages, quashes dowry FIR Prayagraj, The Allahabad High Court has warned that routinely turning every distressed or failed marriage into a criminal case could affect the institution of marriage at its core, quashing an FIR alleging dowry harassment, physical assault and attempted strangulation in a case involving a brief period of cohabitation. A division bench of Justices Chandra Dhari Singh and Tarun Saxena quashed the FIR registered at the Hari Parvat police station in Agra under various provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Dowry Prohibition Act, allowing a writ petition filed by Gaurav Jain and his family members. Emphasising the dangers of converting matrimonial discord intro criminal cases, the court cautioned against the misuse of criminal law in short-lived marriages. According to the facts of the case, the marriage was solemnised on November 12, 2024, and the wife left the matrimonial home on February 3, 2025, after approximately two-and-a-half months of cohabitation. The husband filed a divorce petition on May 3, 2025, following which the FIR was registered on June 30, 2025. The FIR alleged dowry demands and harassment, denial of food, threats, retention of the wife's stridhan and an attempt to strangulate her. The court noted that no domestic violence complaint, police control room call or contemporaneous police intervention concerning the alleged acts had been brought on record from the period of cohabitation. The high court observed that while protecting women from dowry-related violence and cruelty is a statutory and constitutional imperative, the possibility of misuse of criminal law cannot be ignored. It emphasised that matrimnial discord can not automatically be treated as criminality and that criminal proceedings cannot be used as a substitute for adjudication before a matrimonial court. The high court warned that if every distressed or failed marriage is routinely converted into an FIR and subjected to the coercive machinery of criminal law, the institution of marriage will inevitably be affected at its core. In its judgment dated October 8, the high court clarified that its decision did not adjudicate the merits of the pending matrimonial proceedings. Both parties remain free topursue their remedies before the competent matrimonial court. The complainant may also pursue any independent remedy available under the law in respect of a distinct cause of action, subject to statutory requirements. Khandu has convened the meeting with representatives of the ABK Youth Wing and the Adi Students' Union. Accusing the state government of adopting a high-handed approach towards indigenous communities opposing the project, SIFFYW said there should be no dialogue unless FIRs against villagers and activists involved in anti-dam protests and Central Armed Police Forces deployed in the Siang region are withdrawn. SIFFYW called upon community organisations, student unions, clan representatives and political leaders to refrain from engaging with the government over the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project under the guise of consultations. It asserted that there cannot be any dialogue while protesters were behind bars and their grievances were not resolved. Anti-dam activist and SIFFYW legal advisor Ebo Mili said, "What's the point of them meeting with the chief minister? He maintained that the chief minister was free to meet any Adi organisation, community-based organisation or student union on other issues but not SUMP. news.headline: Adhikari launches Durga Puja festivities, cites adherence to religious norms
news.story_lead: Adhikari launches Durga Puja festivities, cites adherence to religious norms This is the first Durga Puja since the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) came to power in May this year, ousting the Trinamool Congress government West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Saturday launched the festivities centred around this year’s Durga Puja, the biggest festival for people in the eastern state, at a grand ceremony at the Netaji Indoor Stadium in Kolkata. “Our government decided that the Durga Puja (festivities) cannot be initiated during the Pitru Paksha phase. That’s why it is being launched today, as the Devi Paksha has begun.
news.full_article_text: Adhikari launches Durga Puja festivities, cites adherence to religious norms This is the first Durga Puja since the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) came to power in May this year, ousting the Trinamool Congress government West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Saturday launched the festivities centred around this year’s Durga Puja, the biggest festival for people in the eastern state, at a grand ceremony at the Netaji Indoor Stadium in Kolkata. “Our government decided that the Durga Puja (festivities) cannot be initiated during the Pitru Paksha phase. That’s why it is being launched today, as the Devi Paksha has begun. On one hand, we decided to maintain the cultural tradition of the Durga Puja; on the other hand, we decided to adhere to the religious norms and our scriptures,” he said. This is the first Durga Puja since the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) came to power in May this year, ousting the Trinamool Congress government. Former CM Mamata Banerjee faced criticism in 2025 from the opposition and some religious and Hindu rights organisations for inaugurating puja pandals before Mahalaya, which marks the transition from Pitru Paksha to Devi Paksha. “Till last year, around 45,000 community pujas were organised by various clubs and organisations across the state. This year, the number has jumped by around 12,400. Earlier, people had to approach the Calcutta high court to seek permission to organise Durga Puja. This year, there has been no such instance to my knowledge,” Adhikari said while addressing the programme, which was attended by an audience of around 40,000. West Bengal governor RN Ravi, ministers, senior bureaucrats and leaders from various spiritual organisations attended the programme. Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen also attended the event. The dignitaries first attended a roadshow led by Adhikari and then attended the grand ceremony. Apart from the cultural programmes, at least 3,000 drones lit up the sky over the stadium, depicting Goddess Durga and scenes including the traditional Dhunuchi Naach. The state tourism department and the information and cultural affairs department will organise special cultural programmes in various cities and tourist destinations, including one on Digha beach, over the next four days before the main Puja celebrations begin. The new BJP government in the state had earlier reduced the grant for Durga Puja committees from 110,000 provided last year by the previous Mamata Banerjee-led government to ₹ 100,000 this year. It also announced a complete ban on DJs during the festivities and the closure of liquor outlets and bars on Maha Ashtami. The Durga Puja carnival, a pet project of Banerjee, has also been cancelled this year.

news.headline: 'Will come back stronger': CJP's Ajinkya Shinde calls fresh protest after Delhi Police crackdown on Jantar Mantar stir
news.story_lead: 'Will come back stronger': CJP's Ajinkya Shinde calls fresh protest after Delhi Police crackdown on Jantar Mantar stir CJP's Ajinkya Shinde calls fresh protest after Delhi Police crackdown on Jantar Mantar stir Cockroach Janta Party leader Ajinkya Shinde on Saturday gave a fresh call for protest to demand the resignation of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the electoral rolls. In a press conference held after a day of unrest in Delhi, where over 4,000 protesters were detained by the Delhi Police in a major crackdown on CJP's call for protest at the Jantar Mantar. news.headline: Delhi Police clarify after video shows cops wearing shoes on Bangla Sahib premises, allege 'malicious intent'
news.story_lead: Delhi Police clarify after video shows cops wearing shoes on Bangla Sahib premises, allege 'malicious intent' The Delhi Police said that legal action was being initiated against those circulating the video showing the cops in bad light. The Delhi Police on Saturday issued a clarification after purported videos on social media showed police officials allegedly enter the premises of Gurdwara Bangla Sahib wearing shoes. The police clarified that the officials were “walking in the common passage” which was used by all devotees to reach the entry point of the Gurdwara.
news.full_article_text: Delhi Police clarify after video shows cops wearing shoes on Bangla Sahib premises, allege 'malicious intent' The Delhi Police said that legal action was being initiated against those circulating the video showing the cops in bad light. The Delhi Police on Saturday issued a clarification after purported videos on social media showed police officials allegedly enter the premises of Gurdwara Bangla Sahib wearing shoes. The police clarified that the officials were “walking in the common passage” which was used by all devotees to reach the entry point of the Gurdwara. Sharing a video of the Bangla Sahib, the Delhi Police said the passage led to the point where shoes were taken off before entering the place of worship. “The process is the same for all devotees coming to Gurdwara. The video showing the same is attached,” it clarified. The Delhi Police alleged that the video circulated on social media had “malicious intent” and was aimed at “outraging the feelings of a respectable religious community”. Deep Dive The police said that legal action was being initiated against those circulating the video showing the cops in bad light. The video came as Delhi Police teams were deployed outside the Gurdwara to nab protesters taking part in the anti-CEC agitation called by the Cockroach Janta Party on October 10. The Delhi Police on Saturday launched a massive crackdown across the city and detained over 4,000 people in view of the anti-CEC stir and CJP's call for march to Jantar Mantar. People around the proposed protest site were bundled away in buses, which included Yashaswinee Raje Singh, daughter of former Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MLA Vikram Singh from Uttar Pradesh. in a post on X, Yashaswinee said that she was detained ‘near Bangla Sahib for sitting in a park’ "Currently being held in Keshav Puram police station,” she wrote on X. news.headline: Mamata Banerjee, Arvind Kejriwal among 4 ex-CMs detained in Delhi's anti-CEC protest crackdown
news.story_lead: Mamata Banerjee, Arvind Kejriwal among 4 ex-CMs detained in Delhi's anti-CEC protest crackdown The detentions took place at multiple locations across Delhi amid heavy security in view of the demonstration called by the CJP against SIR. Several INDIA bloc leaders, including former chief ministers Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee , Pinarayi Vijayan and Manik Sarkar were detained by Delhi Police on Saturday as they attempted to join the protest at Jantar Mantar demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls. Track live updates on Delhi protest The detentions took place at multiple locations across the capital amid heavy security, barricades and restrictions on movement in view of the demonstration called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
news.full_article_text: Mamata Banerjee, Arvind Kejriwal among 4 ex-CMs detained in Delhi's anti-CEC protest crackdown The detentions took place at multiple locations across Delhi amid heavy security in view of the demonstration called by the CJP against SIR. Several INDIA bloc leaders, including former chief ministers Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee , Pinarayi Vijayan and Manik Sarkar were detained by Delhi Police on Saturday as they attempted to join the protest at Jantar Mantar demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls. Track live updates on Delhi protest The detentions took place at multiple locations across the capital amid heavy security, barricades and restrictions on movement in view of the demonstration called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Deep Dive Besides Kejriwal, Banerjee, Vijayan and Sarkar, others detained included CPI(M) general secretary M A Baby, veteran Left leader Brinda Karat, CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya, activist Yogendra Yadav and lawyer Prashant Bhushan . Also read: Supreme Court to hear on Sunday pleas against violation of order on Delhi curbs, detention of Opposition leaders Kejriwal was detained outside his Lodhi Estate residence while marching towards Jantar Mantar with AAP leaders and workers. As police personnel moved to take him away, party workers tried to prevent his detention. Police personnel lifted him by his legs and chest and carried him towards a police bus. Those party leaders detained with him included Rajya Sabha member Sanjay Singh, Delhi unit chief Saurabh Bharadwaj, MLA Kuldeep Kumar and national media in-charge Anurag Dhanda. Senior AAP leader Gopal Rai was also detained while protesting at the party office. "... Till now, Modi ji used to win elections only by stealing votes. Now he has been caught red-handed," he said. "Wherever Modi ji stops you, sit there. Turn that place into Jantar Mantar. Make the whole country a Jantar Mantar," he said. After being detained, Kejriwal demanded Kumar's resignation, saying, "The youth of the country is awake. They are not afraid of Modi ji's tyranny. Banerjee, accompanied by TMC leaders Derek O'Brien, Dola Sen, Samirul Islam, Pratima Mondal and Saket Gokhale, wore a band-aid over her mouth during the protest. news.headline: Rahul Gandhi meets Tamil Nadu CM Vijay in Chennai, allies head for coffee and tiramisu after political talks
news.story_lead: Rahul Gandhi meets Tamil Nadu CM Vijay in Chennai, allies head for coffee and tiramisu after political talks Rahul Gandhi and Vijay visited Bask by Coffee, a cafe, and reportedly had a cappuccino, tiramisu, and cookies. Leader of the opposition (LoP) in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, and Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay reportedly met in Chennai on Saturday. Following their meeting, the two leaders stepped away for a cafe outing, with coffee, cookies and tiramisu on the menu.
news.full_article_text: Rahul Gandhi meets Tamil Nadu CM Vijay in Chennai, allies head for coffee and tiramisu after political talks Rahul Gandhi and Vijay visited Bask by Coffee, a cafe, and reportedly had a cappuccino, tiramisu, and cookies. Leader of the opposition (LoP) in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, and Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay reportedly met in Chennai on Saturday. Following their meeting, the two leaders stepped away for a cafe outing, with coffee, cookies and tiramisu on the menu. Gandhi met TVK chief Vijay at his suburban Neelankarai residence, news agency PTI reported, citing party sources. During the meeting, the two leaders discussed several political issues. Gandhi and Vijay stepped out of the residence and chose to walk together surrounded by heavy security, a senior functionary in the TVK stated, the report added. Also Read | ‘Afraid of Vijay?’ DMK takes jibe at Rahul, asks him to clarify stand on SIR in Tamil Nadu Cappuccino, tiramisu, and cookies Following the meeting, Gandhi and Vijay visited Bask by Coffee, a cafe in the neighbourhood. The two leaders had a cappuccino, tiramisu, and cookies, the report added. The Congress leader then proceeded to a hotel in Chennai. Also Read | CM Vijay hails Dharapuram victory against 'defamatory remarks on women'; Stalin slams ‘temporary win for betrayal’ What Rahul Gandhi and Vijay discussed in meeting According to the report, party sources noted that Gandhi and Vijay discussed long-term political cooperation within their state alliance. Although there is no official statement on their meetings, it added. Here are some of the topics reportedly touched upon in the meeting: - Structural alignment and coordinating governance policies between the Congress and the TVK - Youth-centric issues such as unemployment and education reforms - Local opposition to the NEET examination - Opposition to Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise and allegations of voter roll discrepancies Also Read | Tamil Nadu CM Vijay rides bullock cart during Dharapuram bypoll campaign, interacts with voters | Watch 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' event In the evening, Congress leader Gandhi travelled to the Island Grounds for the youth outreach programme, 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' (Maanavargalin Kural) event. According to a police official cited in the report, access to the event is restricted to QR code entry. Earlier in the day, Congress MP Manickam Tagore said that more than one lakh students had registered online for the 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' interaction programme, news agency ANI reported. “This time he's coming for a student interaction program in Tamil Nadu, where tonight in the evening he's going to address the students of Tamil Nadu. More than a lakh students, one lakh students have registered on the online QR code registration,” Tagore said. "Without a QR code, we are not going to allow anybody. And there are restrictions we have put on those selection processes also, who are going to be the students who are going to be entering here," the Congress MP added. Leader of the opposition (LoP) in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, and Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay reportedly met in Chennai on Saturday. Following their meeting, the two leaders stepped away for a cafe outing, with coffee, cookies and tiramisu on the menu.
Gandhi met TVK chief Vijay at his suburban Neelankarai residence, news agency PTI reported, citing party sources. During the meeting, the two leaders discussed several political issues.
Gandhi and Vijay stepped out of the residence and chose to walk together surrounded by heavy security, a senior functionary in the TVK stated, the report added.

In a post on X, CJP demanded Dipke’s release and questioned his whereabouts: “Where is Abhijeet?
news.full_article_text: CJP asks ‘where is Abhijeet’ after Delhi Police say Dipke was informed of grandmother’s death CJP's post came after the Delhi Police posted on X saying Dipke had been informed about his grandmother’s death and the scheduled time of her funeral. The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has questioned the Delhi Police over its handling of detained party founder Abhijeet Dipke’s request to speak to his family, saying his relatives want to talk to him ahead of his grandmother’s last rites scheduled for Sunday morning. In a post on X, CJP demanded Dipke’s release and questioned his whereabouts: “Where is Abhijeet? His family wants to talk to him, they’re going to perform his grandmother’s last rites tomorrow morning. The least they deserve is to talk to him.” The post came after the Delhi Police posted on X saying Dipke had been informed about his grandmother’s death and the scheduled time of her funeral. The police also said he had been offered assistance to travel to his hometown on humanitarian grounds. Deep Dive “The unfortunate information, regarding the death of his grandmother and known time of her funeral was immediately shared with Sh. Abhijeet Dipke,” the Delhi Police said in its post on X. It added that he had also been offered possible facilitation for his journey home. Nearly 4,000 detained in Delhi Nearly 4,000 people have been detained in Delhi in view of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)'s Jantar Mantar protest today, the police said. Former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal, TMC's Mamata Banerjee and AISA's Neha Bora are among those who were detained in the national capital on Saturday. There were also reports of journalists being detained around Jantar Mantar. Posts and videos on social media showed the detained journalists flashing their press cards from the buses. Wangchuk warns of hunger strike Activist Sonam Wangchuk on Saturday warned of going on another hunger strike if the leaders detained during Saturday's crackdown on anti-CEC protest are not released by tomorrow. In a video message released on his social media handles, the activist claimed that the country was in a state of "undeclared emergency". "Yesterday when I posted a message appealing for unity and peace in today's protest, I had never imagined that the biggest democracy in the world would be under an undeclared EMERGENCY," he wrote. Wangchuk, who extended his support to the anti-CEC protest, was unable to physically take part in the agitation in Delhi. "I was happy there were so many leaders to lead the movement, but I now learn that they have all been arrested," he said. Several INDIA bloc leaders, including former chief ministers Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee, Pinarayi Vijayan and Manik Sarkar were detained by Delhi Police on Saturday as they attempted to join the protest at Jantar Mantar demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Shivya Kanojia Shivya Kanojia is a journalist at Hindustan Times, where she works in the fast-paced digital news ecosystem with a strong sense of editorial judgement and a clear understanding of what makes a story both important and traffic-driven. news.headline: DMRC reopens all Delhi Metro station gates, train services to run as per normal schedule
news.story_lead: DMRC reopens all Delhi Metro station gates, train services to run as per normal schedule The protest was called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which is demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. All entry and exit gates at Delhi Metro stations have been reopened, with train services set to operate as per the normal schedule following temporary restrictions imposed ahead of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protest. The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) said on Saturday that passengers could enter and exit stations as usual.
news.full_article_text: DMRC reopens all Delhi Metro station gates, train services to run as per normal schedule The protest was called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which is demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. All entry and exit gates at Delhi Metro stations have been reopened, with train services set to operate as per the normal schedule following temporary restrictions imposed ahead of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protest. The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) said on Saturday that passengers could enter and exit stations as usual. In a post on X, it also confirmed that interchange facilities at all affected stations had been restored, allowing commuters to switch between metro lines as normal. Several Delhi-bound trains were suspended in view of the protest on October 10. DMRC had also earlier announced that entry and exit gates at 45 metro stations, including Rajiv Chowk, New Delhi, Central Secretariat, Patel Chowk and Kashmere Gate, will remain closed from 9 pm on Friday, October 9, until further notice due to the protest. bullet_points: DMRC reopens all Delhi Metro station gates, train services to run as per normal schedule
The protest was called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which is demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.

All entry and exit gates at Delhi Metro stations have been reopened, with train services set to operate as per the normal schedule following temporary restrictions imposed ahead of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protest.

The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) said on Saturday that passengers could enter and exit stations as usual. In a post on X, it also confirmed that interchange facilities at all affected stations had been restored, allowing commuters to switch between metro lines as normal.
Several Delhi-bound trains were suspended in view of the protest on October 10.

DMRC had also earlier announced that entry and exit gates at 45 metro stations, including Rajiv Chowk, New Delhi, Central Secretariat, Patel Chowk and Kashmere Gate, will remain closed from 9 pm on Friday, October 9, until further notice due to the protest.

The CJP has said that it will resume its Jantar Mantar march tomorrow and will stay there till their demands are met. This was announced by Ajinkya Shinde, the CJP leader who is leading the charge after the detention of Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. Shinde also raised concern over the safety of the detained CJP leaders and said that the whereabouts of the trio is unknown after the police took them away from the plane soon after it landed at the Delhi airport.

Nearly 4,000 people have been detained in Delhi in view of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)'s Jantar Mantar protest today, the police said. Former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal, TMC's Mamata Banerjee and AISA's Neha Bora are among those who were detained in the national capital on Saturday. There were also reports of journalists being detained around Jantar Mantar. Posts and videos on social media showed the detained journalists flashing their press cards from the buses.

news.headline: Delhi protest: Right-wing groups assault protesters, journalists amid heavy security deployment
news.story_lead: Delhi protest: Right-wing groups assault protesters, journalists amid heavy security deployment Many of the men were seen beating protesters in front of police personnel, including instances at Connaught Place that unfolded in front of HT reporters. Groups of men from right-wing organisations threatened and assaulted protesters and journalists in Connaught Place and near the MCD Civic Centre on Saturday, even as more than 25,000 security personnel held the centre of the Capital against the protest. Also Read | Entry and exit gates at all Delhi metro stations reopened, interchange facilities restored: DMRC Near Palika Bazaar at 2.30pm, a group of more than 30 men who said they were from the Bajrang Dal shouted slogans and threatened journalists.
news.full_article_text: Delhi protest: Right-wing groups assault protesters, journalists amid heavy security deployment Many of the men were seen beating protesters in front of police personnel, including instances at Connaught Place that unfolded in front of HT reporters. Groups of men from right-wing organisations threatened and assaulted protesters and journalists in Connaught Place and near the MCD Civic Centre on Saturday, even as more than 25,000 security personnel held the centre of the Capital against the protest. Also Read | Entry and exit gates at all Delhi metro stations reopened, interchange facilities restored: DMRC Near Palika Bazaar at 2.30pm, a group of more than 30 men who said they were from the Bajrang Dal shouted slogans and threatened journalists. "You all are showing fake news for CJP. We will protect Delhi Police since they can't use arms against you," one of them shouted. Police chased the men away and detained some of them half an hour later. Deep Dive Near the MCD Civic Centre, a confrontation between protesters and men from the Hindustan Raksha Dal turned violent when the men began dragging, assaulting and threatening women and men on the street. Also Read | CJP asks ‘where is Abhijeet’ after Delhi Police say Dipke was informed of grandmother’s death In one video of an assault at the location, which spread widely on social media within hours, protesters were seen being slapped, kicked and assaulted. The video, which HT has not verified, showed a young woman being dragged and beaten by two men until her sister pulls her away. "Nobody came to save me. Delhi police saw everything," the woman says in the video. Senior Delhi Police officers said police had rescued the woman, helped her and removed the men from the spot. No FIR has been filed against the men at the time of reporting. HT reached out to the Bajrang Dal, several Delhi Police spokespersons and the deputy commissioner of police (New Delhi), but received no response. In another video, purportedly shot near Connaught Place, men attack a protester with brass knuckles and tear his T-shirt. A 21-year-old media student from Shahdara, who was hiding at Gurdwara Bangla Sahib and declined to be named, said he and two friends had been targeted by both the police and the men. "My two friends and I have been facing assault because of police as well as these right wing goons. They entered the protest not once but thrice since last night. Police didn't even stop them. They hit my friend on the head but he managed to escape. We were making videos as we are media students. But they threatened to beat us and hurled abuses. My friend was near Civic Centre when they assaulted a couple of people. We left in fear," he said. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Jignasa Sinha Jignasa Sinha is a Special Correspondent at Hindustan Times in New Delhi. With more than six years of reporting experience, she covers crime and policing in the national capital. Her beats also include Delhi prisons, the Delhi Fire Services and Delhi courts, while she regularly reports on gender, labour and social justice. Over the course of her career, Jignasa has reported on major criminal investigations, international crime syndicates, high-profile cyber fraud cases, law-and-order developments, protests, disasters and public institutions. Her reporting combines breaking news with in-depth, long form, human interest stories that examine the human impact of public policy, policing and the criminal justice system. In addition to reporting for the newspaper, she contributes to the Hindustan Times website and app, and plays an active role in coordinating on-ground coverage of major developments and breaking news across Delhi. Before joining Hindustan Times, Jignasa worked at The Indian Express newspaper in New Delhi, where she spent five years covering crime, Delhi airport, courts and health. She began her journalism career as an intern at an AI magazine in Bengaluru while pursuing her postgraduate diploma in multimedia journalism at the Indian Institute of Journalism and New Media. news.headline: CJP renews protest call as Abhijeet Dipke, Dhruv Rathee remain detained; Delhi Police cite ‘broken promises’ amid crackdown
news.story_lead: CJP renews protest call as Abhijeet Dipke, Dhruv Rathee remain detained; Delhi Police cite ‘broken promises’ amid crackdown Delhi Police reportedly released all the detainees from the detention centers except CJP leaders. This comes amid a widespread crackdown in national capital. Delhi on Saturday witnessed a major crackdown on a planned protest and the detention of thousands, including four former chief ministers, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijit Dipke, and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee.
news.full_article_text: CJP renews protest call as Abhijeet Dipke, Dhruv Rathee remain detained; Delhi Police cite ‘broken promises’ amid crackdown Delhi Police reportedly released all the detainees from the detention centers except CJP leaders. This comes amid a widespread crackdown in national capital. Delhi on Saturday witnessed a major crackdown on a planned protest and the detention of thousands, including four former chief ministers, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijit Dipke, and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee. The action came amid CJP's call for protest against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, who faces allegations of carrying out irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise. While the police released all the protesters after day-long detention, CJP leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das, and Youtuber Dhruv Rathee remained in custody. The Cockroach Janta Party has given a fresh call for protest, urging people to begin march to Jantar Mantar at 10 am on Sunday. Why Delhi Police stalled protests The Delhi Police shared a video on X, explaining the reason for denying permission to hold the protest at Jantar Mantar. In the caption, the police wrote, "Broken promises, shattered trust." Deep Dive In the video, Delhi Police highlighted that the CJP failed to abide by its signed undertaking while protesting in June-July to demand the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged examination irregularities. Also Read | BJP leader's daughter detained near Bangla Sahib amid CJP protest in Delhi: ‘For sitting in a park’ Key developments from protests against CEC From the closure of 45 metro stations in the national capital to the detention of actor Imran Khan in Mumbai, Saturday saw escalating developments as protests erupted in various parts of the country. 4 ex-CMs detained: Several opposition leaders, including former chief ministers Arvind Kejriwal (AAP), Mamata Banerjee (TMC), Pinarayi Vijayan (CPI-M) and Manik Sarkar (CPI-M), were detained from multiple locations across Delhi as they attempted to join the protest. Abhijeet Dipke and others detained: Dipke and two CJP leaders, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, were detained by Delhi Police from inside an aircraft as soon as their flight landed. Dhruv Rathee detained from Gurugram: YouTuber Rathee, who lives abroad and had come to join the CJP protest, was detained by police from his residence in Gurugram. CJP's Ajinkya Shinde calls fresh protest: Following the detentions, CJP's Ajinkya Shinde has renewed the call for demonstrations on Sunday, October 11. "But we're not backing down! We will march to Jantar Mantar again tomorrow and stay there until all our demands are met," the CJP's post on X read. Tushar Gandhi, actor Imran Khan detained: Police detained actor Imran Khan, activist Tushar Gandhi and CPI (M) workers from various locations in Mumbai for protesting without permission, news agency PTI reported. Sonam Wangchuk's warning: Activist Sonam Wangchuk, in a post shared on his X handle, wrote, "Yesterday when I posted a message appealing for unity & peace in today's protest I had never imagined that the biggest democracy in the world would be under an undeclared EMERGENCY." "I was happy there were so many leaders to lead the movement, but I now learn that they have all been arrested. I hope those arrested will be released soon. I will be compelled to consider an Anshan Fast or Padyatra March if they are not released by tomorrow," he warned. Also Read | Supreme Court to hear on Sunday pleas against violation of order on Delhi curbs, detention of Opposition leaders BJP vs Opposition amid crackdown Earlier on Saturday, BJP national spokesperson Sambit Patra slammed Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and termed him a "nalayak neta" and an "anarchist". Addressing a press conference, Patra criticised the remarks made by Gandhi outside Rashtrapati Bhavan on Friday. "Yesterday a few politicians visited the Rashtrapati Bhavan. The statement of Rahul Gandhi after coming out of the Rashtrapati Bhavan was like that of a 'nalayak neta'... Never before was an attempt made to drag the President into a street protest. But a 'nalayak neta' attempted to do that. The anarchist Rahul Gandhi tried to pull the President of India to anarchism, which he is trying his best to conduct on the streets of India," the BJP leader said. Meanwhile, Congress leader Gandhi, in a post on X, urged the youth to keep protesting. "Youth of India, I am proud of you. Keep protesting. We are standing with you," he wrote. Delhi metro services update Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC), in an X post on Saturday night, informed, “Entry and exit gates of all Metro Stations of the Delhi Metro network are now open. The interchange facility at all the concerned Metro stations is also available.” (with inputs from agencies) - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Anushka Awasthi Anushka Awasthi is a Content Producer at Hindustan Times, where she covers politics, geopolitics, and major national and international developments. She holds both a Bachelor's and a Master's degree in Journalism and Mass Communication from Guru Gobind Singh Indraprastha University (GGSIPU), New Delhi. Passionate about India's political landscape, Anushka believes that politics shapes every aspect of society, from public policy to everyday life. This drives her to deliver timely, accurate, and researched news that helps readers make sense of everyday developments. Before joining Hindustan Times, Anushka worked with the Zee News English website, reporting extensively on Indian politics and international affairs. During her tenure, she also wrote a range of interviews and analytical stories, focusing on key political and international affairs events. Her reporting is driven by a strong interest in journalism and a dedication to balanced reporting. She strives to present news with clarity and context in the digital era. She aims to ensure that readers stay informed about issues that matter. The Cockroach Janta Party has given a fresh call for protest, urging people to begin march to Jantar Mantar at 10 am on Sunday. news.headline: India hits back at UN rights office over remarks on Delhi protests, calls concerns ‘misplaced’
news.story_lead: India hits back at UN rights office over remarks on Delhi protests, calls concerns ‘misplaced’ The Indian embassy said the right to peaceful assembly is constitutionally guaranteed, subject to reasonable restrictions in the interest of public order. India has rejected the UN Human Rights Office’s (OHCHR) remarks on the events in New Delhi, calling its concerns “misplaced” and accusing it of unwarranted interference in the country’s internal affairs. In a statement shared by the Permanent Mission of India to the UN in Geneva on X, India said the right to peaceful assembly was guaranteed by the Constitution and safeguarded by the country’s institutions, an independent judiciary and a free media.
news.full_article_text: India hits back at UN rights office over remarks on Delhi protests, calls concerns ‘misplaced’ The Indian embassy said the right to peaceful assembly is constitutionally guaranteed, subject to reasonable restrictions in the interest of public order. India has rejected the UN Human Rights Office’s (OHCHR) remarks on the events in New Delhi, calling its concerns “misplaced” and accusing it of unwarranted interference in the country’s internal affairs. In a statement shared by the Permanent Mission of India to the UN in Geneva on X, India said the right to peaceful assembly was guaranteed by the Constitution and safeguarded by the country’s institutions, an independent judiciary and a free media. “We have seen the OHCHR’s remarks about today’s events in New Delhi,” the mission said, adding that citizens exercise their right to peaceful assembly subject to reasonable restrictions in the interest of public order. Deep Dive “The authorities, for their part, act in accordance with the law, and our courts remain available to all for redressal of any grievances,” it said. India also called on the OHCHR to devote comparable attention to large-scale protests elsewhere, arguing that the UN body should act in keeping with its mandate of impartiality and non-selectivity. UN raises concerns over Delhi detentions The response came after the United Nations expressed concern over mass detentions in Delhi amid protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The demonstrations have been accompanied by heightened security measures and restrictions in parts of the national capital. The protests, called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and other groups, are linked to demands for Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Delhi Police denied permission for the CJP’s proposed October 10 demonstration at Jantar Mantar, citing short notice, alleged violations during earlier protests and concerns over public safety, traffic and law and order. The restrictions triggered legal scrutiny, with the Supreme Court intervening over curbs affecting public transport and calling for a balance between the right to protest and the need to prevent disruption to essential services. India, in its response to the OHCHR, maintained that authorities acted in accordance with the law and that judicial remedies remained available to those who believed their rights had been violated. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Abhimanyu Kulkarni Abhimanyu Kulkarni has spent over a decade in newsrooms and currently heads the online news desk.
