news.headline: ‘System can’t be honest when you win and rigged when you lose’: 124 ex-bureaucrats defend Election Commission, SIR exercise
news.story_lead: ‘System can’t be honest when you win and rigged when you lose’: 124 ex-bureaucrats defend Election Commission, SIR exercise Defending SIR, the ex-civil servants described it as a necessary process to maintain accurate electoral rolls by identifying deceased voters, duplicate entries After 42 former judges raised concerns over what they described as a sustained campaign against the Election Commission of India (ECI), 124 former bureaucrats have written an open letter defending the poll body amid allegations of irregularities in the electoral process. In their letter to the citizens of India, the 124 former IAS, IFS and allied services officers said the country’s electoral system had undergone a significant transformation from the era of booth capturing, ballot box stuffing and election-related violence. They highlighted safeguards such as polling agents, the sealing of electronic voting m
news.full_article_text: ‘System can’t be honest when you win and rigged when you lose’: 124 ex-bureaucrats defend Election Commission, SIR exercise Defending SIR, the ex-civil servants described it as a necessary process to maintain accurate electoral rolls by identifying deceased voters, duplicate entries After 42 former judges raised concerns over what they described as a sustained campaign against the Election Commission of India (ECI), 124 former bureaucrats have written an open letter defending the poll body amid allegations of irregularities in the electoral process. In their letter to the citizens of India, the 124 former IAS, IFS and allied services officers said the country’s electoral system had undergone a significant transformation from the era of booth capturing, ballot box stuffing and election-related violence. They highlighted safeguards such as polling agents, the sealing of electronic voting machines (EVMs), strong-room security and Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT) verification. Also Read | Delhi protest: Right-wing groups assault protesters, journalists amid heavy security deployment The letter comes amid protests in Delhi and Mumbai against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of electoral irregularities. “A system cannot be honest when you win and rigged when you lose,” the letter stated, according to ANI, noting that the party ruling at the Centre had lost several state elections under the same Election Commission. The officers also referred to the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, in which the ruling party failed to secure an outright majority on its own. Defending the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, the former civil servants described it as a necessary process to maintain accurate electoral rolls by identifying deceased voters, duplicate entries and individuals who had permanently shifted residence. Also Read | 'EC at centre of assault': 42 ex-judges defend India's poll process in open letter amid protest against Gyanesh Kumar They also maintained that the SIR process included safeguards to address concerns over wrongful exclusion, including the publication of draft electoral rolls, opportunities to file claims and objections, hearings and provisions for appeals. “Questioning is every citizen’s right. Proving is the accuser’s duty,” the officers said, adding that unsubstantiated allegations could weaken public confidence in democratic institutions and the electoral process. Also Read | Election Commission tightens limits on Form-7 filings to check bulk objections Meanwhile, in a separate open letter, 42 former judges and retired constitutional officeholders said they had no political brief and were speaking out because “silence is no longer a neutral choice”. They alleged that constitutional bodies were facing attacks driven by political interests and warned of the consequences of undermining public trust in the country’s democratic institutions. “Our concern is grave. India's constitutional bodies are under sustained attack. The Election Commission of India stands at the centre of this assault,” the letter read. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Shubham Pandey Shubham Pandey works as Chief Content Producer at the Hindustan Times online desk, where he writes news articles, explainers, and features with a focus on audience engagement, traffic growth, and real-time storytelling. Defending the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, the former civil servants described it as a necessary process to maintain accurate electoral rolls by identifying deceased voters, duplicate entries and individuals who had permanently shifted residence.

news.headline: Several injured in attack on airport in Saudi capital Riyadh
news.story_lead: A blast was heard at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh - Published 10 October 2026, 16:05 BST Several people have been injured in another attack on an international airport in the Saudi capital Riyadh, authorities say, days after Yemen's Houthis claimed to have carried out similar strikes on the hub. Operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh were suspended on Saturday after the attack, the Saudi Civil Aviation Authority said in a statement. More than a dozen ambulances were seen rushing to the airport, according to news agency Reuters, citing an eyewitness.
news.full_article_text: A blast was heard at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh - Published 10 October 2026, 16:05 BST Several people have been injured in another attack on an international airport in the Saudi capital Riyadh, authorities say, days after Yemen's Houthis claimed to have carried out similar strikes on the hub. Operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh were suspended on Saturday after the attack, the Saudi Civil Aviation Authority said in a statement. More than a dozen ambulances were seen rushing to the airport, according to news agency Reuters, citing an eyewitness. The US embassy said it was "aware of attacks on King Khalid International Airport" and urged American citizens to avoid the airport and surrounding areas. The attack comes a day after authorities said three Saudis including a pilot were killed in two attacks on the airport by the Iran-backed Houthis the day prior. Another three people were killed in Houthi attacks on two Saudi airports on 6 and 7 October. A source at a local hospital told AFP that dozens of people had been wounded in Saturday's attack. "I saw 401 hit, I saw injured in front of my eyes. Everyone was running," an eyewitness who said they had been at gate 401 in the domestic terminal told the news agency. Western embassies in Saudi Arabia have warned their citizens away from the airport, while the UK Foreign Office told British nationals to stay away "until the airport is secure and to monitor the advice of the Saudi authorities". Several Gulf airlines said they had cancelled their flights to and from the airport, with Kuwait Airways citing the "security situation" there. All flights to Riyadh have either been diverted or cancelled, aviation tracker Flightradar shows. Doctors had been asked to report to hospitals to address the situation, a medical source told AFP. "We were told we are dealing with a 'serious emergency situation'," the medical source told the agency. The suspected attack comes during a marked escalation in renewed fighting between Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces and the Houthis, who control most of the country's north-west. The Houthis say they are targeting Saudi Arabia over its support for government forces in Yemen's civil war. The conflict worsened after the Houthis seized strategically important stretches of the Red Sea coast in a rapid offensive. That included the port of Mokha on the Bab al-Mandab Strait, which is the narrowest point of the Red Sea and a chokepoint for global shipping. Yemeni pro-government forces have since said they had "secured" the strait at the southern end of the Red Sea. A Saudi-led coalition was formed in 2015 after Arab countries joined forces to stop the Houthis taking over Yemen from the country's internationally recognised government. A temporary ceasefire was brokered in 2022 after years of air strikes and ground fighting led to the deaths of hundreds of thousands of people, triggering one of the world's worst humanitarian crises. But the informal truce began to unravel in July. The Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea. They said they were retaliating against what they described as a years-long Saudi blockade and for an air strike on Sanaa airport. news.headline: Not just Jantar Mantar, internet suspended at 8 other locations amid CJP protest in Delhi
news.story_lead: Not just Jantar Mantar, internet suspended at 8 other locations amid CJP protest in Delhi The order, approved by Union home secretary Govind Mohan, suspended mobile internet within 500 metres of each site from noon to 10pm on Saturday. The Union home ministry approved the suspension of mobile internet around at least eight places across Delhi that had been designated temporary jails for Saturday's protest, beyond the shutdown around central Delhi, according to records seen by HT. The order, dated October 9 and approved by Union home secretary Govind Mohan, suspended mobile internet within 500 metres of each site from noon to 10pm on Saturday.

The Union home ministry approved the suspension of mobile internet around at least eight places across Delhi that had been designated temporary jails for Saturday's protest, beyond the shutdown around central Delhi, according to records seen by HT. The order, dated October 9 and approved by Union home secretary Govind Mohan, suspended mobile internet within 500 metres of each site from noon to 10pm on Saturday.
hindi_translation.full_article_text: Not just Jantar Mantar, internet suspended at 8 other locations amid CJP protest in Delhi The order, approved by Union home secretary Govind Mohan, suspended mobile internet within 500 metres of each site from noon to 10pm on Saturday. The Union home ministry approved the suspension of mobile internet around at least eight places across Delhi that had been designated temporary jails for Saturday's protest, beyond the shutdown around central Delhi, according to records seen by HT. The order, dated October 9 and approved by Union home secretary Govind Mohan, suspended mobile internet within 500 metres of each site from noon to 10pm on Saturday. "It is necessary and expedient so to do in the interest of public order and for preventing incitement to the commission of any offence," it said. ALSO READ: CJP renews protest call as Abhijeet Dipke, Dhruv Rathee remain detained; Delhi Police cite ‘broken promises’ The sites listed are Chhatrasal Stadium in Model Town, Rajiv Gandhi Stadium in Bawana, the Yamuna Sports Complex in east Delhi, the Jasola Sports Complex in Sarita Vihar, a community centre in Daulatpur, two community centres in Chhawla, Jangli Ram Stadium in Kanjhawala and Surajmal Stadium in Nangloi. Deep Dive The Delhi government had notified the sites as temporary jails or detention centres, and thousands of protesters, including Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activists, were taken to them during the day. Supreme Court lawyers who were detained were taken to the Yamuna Sports Complex, and student activists and leaders of the Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist) to Surajmal Stadium. Delhi Police had asked the ministry on Friday to suspend services to avoid any disruption of law and order. Through the day, residents of east Delhi, away from the New Delhi area, posted on social media that they too were facing internet restrictions and asked whether a ban was in force there. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Prawesh Lama Prawesh Lama, an Associate Editor at Hindustan Times with nearly two decades of frontline reporting experience across India’s conflict zones, border regions, and disaster-hit areas. He writes on internal security, insurgency, the Northeast, and Left-wing extremism and has reported from India’s hinterland and some of the most sensitive and strategically critical regions. news.headline: 'Time for Ukraine to get new president,' says Trump after Zelensky condemns diesel deal
news.story_lead: Watch: 'Time for Ukraine to get a new president', says Trump - Published 10 October 2026, 18:31 BST US President Donald Trump has said he thinks "it's time for Ukraine to get a new president" as he responded to Volodymyr Zelensky's criticism of the US diesel deal with Russia. The Ukrainian president warned a new deal to release millions of tonnes of Russian diesel into the US would provide Moscow with money to continue its war against his nation, calling it a gift to Russian President Vladimir Putin. Trump told reporters outside the White House on Saturday that Zelensky "wants to make problems for the world" by continuing to authorise attacks on Russian refineries.
news.full_article_text: Watch: 'Time for Ukraine to get a new president', says Trump - Published 10 October 2026, 18:31 BST US President Donald Trump has said he thinks "it's time for Ukraine to get a new president" as he responded to Volodymyr Zelensky's criticism of the US diesel deal with Russia. The Ukrainian president warned a new deal to release millions of tonnes of Russian diesel into the US would provide Moscow with money to continue its war against his nation, calling it a gift to Russian President Vladimir Putin. Trump told reporters outside the White House on Saturday that Zelensky "wants to make problems for the world" by continuing to authorise attacks on Russian refineries. "He'd better damn well stop," Trump said, before suggesting Ukraine should "get a new leader who can make a deal". Russia and Ukraine have recently intensified their strikes, targeting energy-generating and transport facilities, as well as major logistics hubs. "We said, 'you can do whatever you want to Russia, don't hit the refineries', because that's a world problem that's caused," he said. "He could have made many deals and for some reason, he never does." Putin's envoy Kirill Dmitriev described Trump's intervention as "iconic and historic", saying that Ukraine "needs leadership actually focused on peace". The US president confirmed on Friday that an agreement had been reached with Moscow to suspend sanctions on Russian diesel exports until 7 April. Zelensky reacted by saying it would allow Moscow to raise new funds to source new military equipment to continue the war. He also accused Moscow of taking the deal "to mean they can keep fighting, to mean they keep dropping bombs on cities" following deadly new strikes on Zaporizhzhia. - Analysis: Trump's shock Russia deal highlights mounting pressure to curb fuel prices Published 20 hours ago The Ukrainian president spoke to several allies on Saturday to discuss the latest developments, calling for "real decisions to protect lives in Ukraine" and to protect European security. A Downing Street spokesperson said UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham had spoken to Zelensky and that the pair had agreed Russia should acquiesce to "an immediate energy ceasefire" and end its attacks on shipping in the Black Sea. "This would immediately release more energy and food supplies into the global market," the spokesperson added. News of the US-Russia diesel deal was also met with criticism by EU's foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas, who echoed Zelensky in saying that suspending sanctions "provides Moscow with more revenues to wage war", adding: "This is not the time to ease pressure on Russia, and Europe won't." She said European foreign ministers intended to approve the biggest set of sanctions on Russia since the start of its full-scale invasion on Monday. The deal with Russia is the latest effort from Trump to lower fuel prices in the US ahead of the midterm elections, after months spent grappling with the political consequences of the Iran war. That conflict, which began in February, has sent the cost of petrol and in particular diesel skyrocketing, which has soured his standing with the American public who have been stung by the higher pump prices and knock-on effects that led to across-the-board inflation. The average price of diesel is currently $6.28 (Â£4.74) a gallon, according to the AAA â up from last month's $5.94 average, and $3.68 last year. Under the deal, Russia would release an initial 300,000 tonnes of diesel "to the American and global marketplace" followed by an additional 500,000 tonnes in November. A further million would follow, Trump wrote on Truth Social, and then another 3m tonnes "within a short period of time" â but he noted that this delivery will be "based on the condition of their diesel refineries". In the past 10 months, Russia experienced two waves of severe fuel shortages across the country due to Ukrainian drones strikes on its oil refineries. Diesel production in Russia dropped by an estimated 30%, according to the International Energy Agency. Trump had already called for new elections in Ukraine last December , external , saying Ukrainian voters should have the choice to replace Zelensky. Since the war broke out in 2022 Ukraine has been under martial law, meaning elections are suspended. news.full_article_text: Supreme Court to hear on Sunday pleas against violation of order on Delhi curbs, detention of Opposition leaders A special Bench comprising Justices Bagchi and Mohana will hear the matter. The plea alleges that authorities failed to comply with the court’s directions Trinamool Congress MP and senior advocate Menaka Guruswamy has moved the Supreme Court challenging the preventive detention of Opposition leaders, including four former chief ministers, and other individuals during Saturday’s protests in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar , prompting a special sitting of the court on Sunday. A bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana will hear the matter on October 11, along with a separate contempt petition alleging that authorities failed to comply with the Supreme Court ’s Friday order against a blanket shutdown of Metro and railway services ahead of the demonstrations. Track live updates from Delhi protests TMC MP questions detention of protestors, Oppn leaders Guruswamy has questioned the police action of picking up protesters from the streets and Opposition leaders from their residences, arguing that preventive detention cannot be used to suppress the fundamental right to peaceful protest, particularly when it involves political leaders who have previously governed states. The petition follows Saturday’s crackdown on a protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and other political groups at Jantar Mantar, demanding Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. Delhi Police had denied permission for the demonstration, citing security considerations. The court will also consider a contempt plea filed by advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi against Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) chairperson D Thara, alleging that the authorities failed to implement its October 9 directions on public transport and traffic management. Also Read | 'Don't use hammer to kill a fly': Supreme Court asks Centre, Delhi Police to lift blanket curbs on metro, trains The petition, filed through advocate Chand Qureshi, contends that despite the Supreme Court’s order requiring the authorities to ensure that commuters were not inconvenienced, 57 Metro stations remained subject to closure restrictions, several trains scheduled to arrive at or depart from New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin stations were cancelled, and no traffic advisory was published in newspapers. news.story_lead: Prakash Rajpurohit named deputy election commissioner in bureaucratic reshuffle A 2010-batch IAS officer from the Rajasthan cadre, he replaced Sanjay Kumar as deputy election commissioner Senior bureaucrat Prakash Rajpurohit was appointed deputy election commissioner in a major bureaucratic reshuffle by the Centre on Saturday. Rajpurohit was most recently joint secretary in the Department of Defence Production. He earlier served as director in the Department of Economic Affairs, handling international investment treaties, and held district and tax administration postings in Rajasthan, including as Collector of Ajmer and Commissioner of Commercial Taxes.
news.full_article_text: Prakash Rajpurohit named deputy election commissioner in bureaucratic reshuffle A 2010-batch IAS officer from the Rajasthan cadre, he replaced Sanjay Kumar as deputy election commissioner Senior bureaucrat Prakash Rajpurohit was appointed deputy election commissioner in a major bureaucratic reshuffle by the Centre on Saturday. Rajpurohit was most recently joint secretary in the Department of Defence Production. He earlier served as director in the Department of Economic Affairs, handling international investment treaties, and held district and tax administration postings in Rajasthan, including as Collector of Ajmer and Commissioner of Commercial Taxes. A 2010-batch IAS officer from the Rajasthan cadre, he replaced Sanjay Kumar as deputy election commissioner, according to a Personnel Ministry order. His tenure extends until April 8, 2030. Vivek Khare, a 1996-batch Indian Telecom Service officer, will serve as joint secretary at the National Testing Agency (NTA). His overall tenure runs until December 2, 2029. With Khare’s appointment, four joint secretaries have now been appointed to the NTA since May 16. The other three are Anshuman Sharma, Anuja Bapat and Ruchita Vij. The appointments are part of the NTA’s restructuring, in line with the recommendations of the October 2024 Radhakrishnan committee, which called for strengthening the agency’s permanent manpower to improve accountability. The government subsequently created 16 new posts. The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet cleared 27 appointments of IAS, IRS and other officers to joint secretary-level and equivalent posts. The orders cover institutions including the Election Commission, the National Health Authority, the NTA, NITI Aayog, the Central Vigilance Commission and the National Commission for Women. Officers placed in the Ministry of Home Affairs include Ravi Shankar (IAS, Gujarat, 2007), Chittaranjan Dash (IRS, 1999), P. Manoj Kumar (ISS, 1998) and Abhishek Bhagotia (IAS, Assam-Meghalaya, 2007). In other postings, Tanvi Sundriyal (IAS, Madhya Pradesh, 2010) has been named joint secretary in the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, while Inderjeet Singh (IAS, Rajasthan, 2010) has been appointed to the Ministry of Culture. Navin Agarwal (IRPS, 1997) goes to the Department of Legal Affairs, while Sonia Pant (IES, 2001) becomes Adviser at NITI Aayog.

Rajpurohit was most recently joint secretary in the Department of Defence Production. He earlier served as director in the Department of Economic Affairs, handling international investment treaties, and held district and tax administration postings in Rajasthan, including as Collector of Ajmer and Commissioner of Commercial Taxes. A 2010-batch IAS officer from the Rajasthan cadre, he replaced Sanjay Kumar as deputy election commissioner, according to a Personnel Ministry order. His tenure extends until April 8, 2030. Vivek Khare, a 1996-batch Indian Telecom Service officer, will serve as joint secretary at the National Testing Agency (NTA). His overall tenure runs until December 2, 2029. With Khare’s appointment, four joint secretaries have now been appointed to the NTA since May 16. The other three are Anshuman Sharma, Anuja Bapat and Ruchita Vij. The appointments are part of the NTA’s restructuring, in line with the recommendations of the October 2024 Radhakrishnan committee, which called for strengthening the agency’s permanent manpower to improve accountability. The government subsequently created 16 new posts. The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet cleared 27 appointments of IAS, IRS and other officers to joint secretary-level and equivalent posts. The orders cover institutions including the Election Commission, the National Health Authority, the NTA, NITI Aayog, the Central Vigilance Commission and the National Commission for Women. Officers placed in the Ministry of Home Affairs include Ravi Shankar (IAS, Gujarat, 2007), Chittaranjan Dash (IRS, 1999), P. Manoj Kumar (ISS, 1998) and Abhishek Bhagotia (IAS, Assam-Meghalaya, 2007). In other postings, Tanvi Sundriyal (IAS, Madhya Pradesh, 2010) has been named joint secretary in the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, while Inderjeet Singh (IAS, Rajasthan, 2010) has been appointed to the Ministry of Culture. Navin Agarwal (IRPS, 1997) goes to the Department of Legal Affairs, while Sonia Pant (IES, 2001) becomes Adviser at NITI Aayog.
